paper.title: RePro: Proof-Verified Benchmark Rewriting for Reliable Evaluation of LLM Mathematical Problem Solving
paper.abstract: Data contamination undermines the reliable evaluation of large language models (LLMs) on mathematical problem solving. While rewriting-based evaluation mitigates memorization, existing methods lack guarantees of problem validity and answer correctness. We propose Proof-Verified Benchmark Rewriting (RePro), the first framework to integrate Lean-oriented neural automated theorem provers (ATPs) into benchmark rewriting, which rewrites problems and regenerates answers with correctness ensured by Lea

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是“重写式数学评测不可靠”这个很具体但很关键的问题。现有去污染评测常把原题改写后再测模型，以降低训练集记忆带来的高分；但改写后的题目常出现两个硬伤：题意本身不再严谨，或者参考答案已经错了。前者会让评测对象变成一堆语义含混、约束冲突、不可解的问题；后者更直接，会把模型答对判成错，或者把答错判成对。RePro要解决的不是单纯多生成一些改写题，而是构造一套能对“题目是否定义良好、是否可行、答案是否正确”给出机器可验证保证的重写流程，尤其面向可形式化的数学题。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的意义主要在评测侧，而不是训练方法侧。它提供了一种更干净的数学能力测量方式，用来区分“模型真的会推理”与“模型见过类似题”。这对做数据去污、训练数据成员推断、推理能力真实性分析都很重要。贡献量级上，它不是改变模型训练范式的工作，但在数学评测可靠性上补上了一个长期缺口：过去很多重写 benchmark 只是降低表面重复，却没有保证改写后样本仍然成立。RePro把 Lean 验证引入重写管线后，至少在保留下来的样本上，把参考答案正确性从启发式判断提升到了形式证明支持。这使它更像一个高精度评测资产构建方法，而不是普通的数据增强。
summary.technical_approach:
方法设计是一个三阶段、逐步收紧的验证管线。第一阶段是 LLM 重写。模型对原题做数值重参数化、逻辑重组、约束修改、语境重构等改写，但被明确要求不要直接求解新题，目的是把“题目生成”和“答案生成”解耦，减少模型顺手沿用原答案或在改写时偷偷完成求解。第二阶段是保守语义筛查。这里先过滤掉明显不合格的候选题，比如条件缺失、表述歧义、前提矛盾、现实约束不成立、无解或多解但答案类型仍假定唯一值等。论文强调 feasibility 不是形式逻辑里“能否从前提推出结论”那么窄，而是题目语义和约束是否自洽。第三阶段是形式化与证明验证。候选题被翻译成 Lean 可执行规格，再由 Lean-oriented neural ATP，如 Goedel-Prover、DeepSeek-Prover，搜索候选证明脚本；只有通过 Lean kernel 检查的证明才被接受。这里的关键不是“神经 ATP 会证明”，而是“神经 ATP 只负责提案，最终裁决交给 Lean 内核”。这一步把神经模型的不稳定性关进了 proof assistant 的边界内。

和已有重写评测相比，差异有三点。第一，验证对象从“看起来像对”变成“有形式证明支持的答案”。第二，验证粒度从单一答案核对扩展到 well-definedness、feasibility、answer correctness 三个层面。第三，RePro只保留通过严格验证的样本，接受覆盖率下降来换取高精度。这种取舍很像高质量预训练数据清洗：宁可少，也不要把脏样本混进核心评测集。
summary.experiments:
实验主要在 GSM8K 和 MATH 上做，重点不是追求大规模覆盖，而是比较不同重写方法生成样本的可靠性。论文给出的核心结果是：在保留下来的 rewritten instances 上，RePro 达到 100% 的 well-definedness、feasibility 和 answer correctness；而已有方法即使能生成不少改写题，仍会留下无效题或错误参考答案。这个结果说明 Lean 验证确实改变了 benchmark 质量上限，而不是只做了更严格的人工筛查。

另一条重要实验线是 reformulation sensitivity。作者用 proof-verified rewrites 去测模型在“同一数学结构、不同表述方式”下的性能变化，发现若干模型在经过证明验证的改写题上准确率明显下降。这一点很关键，因为它把性能下降更可信地归因到表述变化和潜在记忆依赖，而不是改写题本身坏掉。论文还讨论了 retained rewritten instances 的概念：不是所有改写都能被形式化并证明，因此最终发布的是通过验证的子集。这个 retained subset 的高精度，是方法成立的前提；代价则是召回率和题型覆盖受限，尤其对难以形式化的自然语言数学题更明显。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时先看 Introduction 和方法总览图，抓住它要解决的不是“怎么改写得更花”，而是“怎么保证改写后还能测”。然后重点看 RePro 方法部分里三阶段流程，尤其 feasibility screening 与 Lean verification 的边界划分：哪些错误在语义筛查阶段处理，哪些错误必须交给形式证明。实验部分建议先看 reliability 对比表，再看 reformulation sensitivity 分析，这两处最能体现方法价值。附录里如果有具体 Lean formalization 示例和失败案例，也值得扫一眼，能帮助判断这套方法的适用边界。预计 25-35 分钟可以抓住主线；若关心数学 benchmark 去污染，可再细看 formalization pipeline 和 retained-rate 相关细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a specific failure mode in contamination-resistant math evaluation: rewritten benchmarks are often not trustworthy. Rewriting a problem can reduce memorization effects, but it also introduces two serious risks: the rewritten problem may become ill-posed, and the regenerated reference answer may be wrong. Once either happens, the benchmark no longer measures reasoning reliably. RePro is designed to build rewritten math benchmarks where the retained instances are not only different from the originals, but also well-defined, feasible, and paired with answers backed by formal proof.
summary_en.importance: Its impact is mainly on evaluation quality rather than on pretraining algorithms. For foundation-model research, this matters because reliable math evaluation is often used to infer whether gains come from genuine reasoning, data overlap, or benchmark leakage. RePro contributes a higher-precision way to construct decontaminated math test sets. The main contribution is not broader coverage, but stronger guarantees: instead of heuristic validation or LLM-as-a-judge checks, it upgrades answer verification to Lean-checked proof support. That makes it useful as an evaluation asset construction method for contamination analysis, reformulation sensitivity studies, and benchmark reliability work.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The method is a staged verification pipeline. First, an LLM rewrites the original problem using strategies such as numerical reparameterization, logical restructuring, constraint modification, and contextual reconstruction. Importantly, the rewriter is instructed not to solve the rewritten problem, which helps separate problem generation from answer generation. Second, RePro performs conservative semantic screening. This stage filters out candidates that are ambiguous, under-specified, contradictory, unrealistic, or infeasible. The paper is careful about the notion of feasibility: it is not merely formal derivability, but semantic and constraint consistency of the rewritten problem. Third, the surviving candidates are translated into executable Lean specifications, and Lean-oriented neural ATPs such as Goedel-Prover and DeepSeek-Prover search for candidate proof scripts. A proof is accepted only if it passes Lean kernel-level verification.

This design differs from prior rewriting-based evaluation in three ways. It verifies answers through formal proof rather than heuristic checking. It evaluates reliability along three axes—well-definedness, feasibility, and answer correctness—rather than treating validity as a single vague notion. And it explicitly trades recall for precision by retaining only proof-verified instances. That trade-off is deliberate and sensible for benchmark construction.
summary_en.experiments:
The experiments are conducted on GSM8K and MATH. The headline result is straightforward: among the retained rewritten instances, RePro achieves 100% well-definedness, feasibility, and answer correctness, whereas prior rewriting methods still leave invalid questions or incorrect reference answers in the benchmark. This is the central empirical claim, and it supports the paper’s argument that formal verification changes the reliability ceiling of rewritten evaluation sets.

A second important result concerns reformulation sensitivity. Using proof-verified rewrites, the authors show that several models suffer noticeable accuracy drops when mathematically equivalent problems are restated in new forms. Because the rewritten items are verified, the drop is more plausibly attributed to sensitivity to formulation and possible memorization dependence, rather than to benchmark corruption. The paper also makes clear that not every rewrite survives the pipeline: the released benchmark is a retained subset of candidates that can be formalized and proved. That gives high precision, but limits coverage and may bias the benchmark toward problems that are easier to formalize in Lean.
summary_en.reading_guide: Start with the introduction and the main pipeline figure. The key idea is not better paraphrasing, but reliable rewritten evaluation. Then read the RePro methodology carefully, especially the boundary between semantic feasibility screening and formal proof verification. That division explains why the system needs both LLM-based filtering and Lean-based checking. In the experiments, focus first on the reliability comparison tables, then on the reformulation-sensitivity analysis. Those sections carry most of the paper’s value. If time permits, inspect the appendix examples of Lean formalization and failure cases; they reveal the practical limits of the approach. A solid skim should take about 30 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 这篇不改模型，但会改你看数学 benchmark 的口径；先看重写保真率和准确率掉幅，很多“推理提升”可能要重算。
recommendation.en: It does not improve models, but it may change how you read math benchmarks; check the rewrite validity and the accuracy drops first—some claimed reasoning gains may need to be discounted.

paper.title: SHAPE of Chain-of-Thought in Math Reasoning
paper.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, yet the mathematically meaningful skills underlying their reasoning remain underexplored. We introduce \texttt{SHAPE}, a framework that analyzes Chain-of-Thought (CoT) trajectories through two lenses developed in mathematics education: (1) semantic spaces: the model's evolving mathematical interpretations of a problem (e.g., algebraic, geometric), and (2) heuristics: the specific mathematical actions ta

summary.core_problem: 数学推理中的 CoT 该如何被“可解释地分解”为数学上有意义的技能单元，并预测正确性来自哪里。
summary.importance: 机制分析贡献：把 CoT 从表层统计特征（长度、困惑度等）推进到“语义空间+启发式动作”的可解释框架；对推理训练信号设计、过程监督/验证器建模有间接启发。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 SHAPE：用数学教育中的两类概念标注/分析 CoT 轨迹——(1) semantic spaces：模型在推理过程中采用的数学表征/视角（代数/几何等）；(2) heuristics：在该空间内采取的具体动作（化简、逆向、分解等）。用这些特征解释/预测最终答案正确性，并分析“集中在少数语义空间深挖”与“到处探索”对成功率的关系。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体模型列表与数据集名称，但声称跨多个模型做 CoT 模式分析；核心结果是：heuristics 特征对正确性解释力强于传统 CoT 特征；正确解往往来自在少数 semantic spaces 内集中推理而非广泛跳转。

summary_en.core_problem: How to decompose math Chain-of-Thought into mathematically meaningful skill units and explain where correctness comes from.
summary_en.importance: A mechanistic/interpretability contribution: moves beyond superficial CoT features (length, etc.) to a semantic-space + heuristic-action framework, with implications for process supervision and verifier design.
summary_en.technical_approach: SHAPE analyzes CoT trajectories using (1) semantic spaces (the mathematical interpretation/representation adopted over time, e.g., algebraic vs geometric) and (2) heuristics (actions within a space, e.g., simplify, work backward). These features are used to explain/predict answer correctness and to study exploration vs concentrated reasoning patterns.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract omits exact model/dataset details, but reports analyses across multiple models. Key findings: heuristic features explain correctness better than traditional CoT features; successful solutions tend to concentrate effort within a few semantic spaces rather than hopping across many.

recommendation.zh: 读它不是为了“更强解题”，而是为了把 CoT 过程监督做得更像技能建模：重点看 heuristics 特征如何预测正确性那部分结论。
recommendation.en: Not a performance paper—use it to think about process supervision as skill modeling; focus on the result that heuristic-level features predict correctness better than surface CoT stats.

paper.title: INSPIRE: An Internalize-Then-Improve Approach for Example-Driven Mathematical Reasoning
paper.abstract: Mathematical reasoning has seen rapid progress in large language models (LLMs), yet existing methods optimize predominantly for final-answer correctness, raising the question whether models truly internalize mathematical concepts or merely memorize solution patterns. In human mathematics education, example-based reasoning such as constructing counterexamples to test theorem boundaries reflects deep conceptual understanding, but remains underdeveloped in current LLMs. Enhancing this capability th

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是一个比“把题做对”更细的问题：如何让模型真正学会以例证驱动的方式做数学推理，而不是只在答案监督下记住证明模板或定理套用路径。作者指出，现有偏好优化大多只看 final answer correctness，这会把“是否主动构造例子、反例、边界情形来检验命题”这一类更接近概念内化的能力压平。难点有两个：一是能力稀缺，基座模型自己采样出来的候选回答在 example-based reasoning 上普遍偏弱，难以形成有质量差异的 preference pair；二是这种能力具有阶段性，模型往往要先学会‘愿意采用这种策略’，再学会‘正确地采用这种策略’，两者很难靠一次性偏好训练同时获得。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接影响不在于提出了新的 pretrain objective，而在于它把“能力形成的阶段性”讲得比较清楚，并给出了一种可操作的 post-train recipe：先做 strategy internalization，再做 correctness refinement。这个思路对 reasoning data synthesis、mid-training、以及面向特定认知策略的 curriculum 都有参考价值。更具体地说，它提醒人们：如果目标能力在当前 policy 分布下几乎不存在，那么直接做 on-policy preference optimization 往往没有足够梯度；但如果完全用外部高质量答案做 chosen，又会引入明显的 style / reasoning-structure shift，模型容易学到表面形式而不是方法本身。作者试图在这两者之间搭桥，这一点比单纯再做一轮 DPO 更有信息量。
summary.technical_approach: 方法核心是 Inspire：Internalize-Then-Improve。它由两部分组成。第一部分是 Reference-Guided Student Internalization（RGSI）。作者先用外部参考解答提供目标推理方式，但不直接把参考答案当作 chosen response，而是让学生模型理解参考中的 reasoning approach，再用自己的表达风格重写生成回答。这样构造出的样本仍然更接近 policy model 的分布，同时又带入了原本缺失的 example-based reasoning 信号，用来缓解 off-policy reference 直接训练带来的分布偏移。第二部分是 stage-wise rubric preference training。作者没有把偏好信号压缩成单一正确率，而是设计了三维 rubric：Method、Reasoning、Correctness。Method 判断是否主动采用例证驱动分析；Reasoning 看论证是否连贯完整；Correctness 看结论是否正确。用 DeepSeek V3.2 作为 judge，分别打分。训练时分阶段推进：先偏重 method-oriented preference，让模型先形成‘会用例子想问题’的倾向；再在此基础上加入 correctness-oriented preference，提升最终答案质量。这个设计和常见一次性 DPO 的区别在于，它显式承认能力获取不是单步完成的，也承认不同维度的 reward signal 可能在早期互相干扰。全文的关键不是某个新损失，而是数据构造和训练顺序的耦合设计。
summary.experiments: 从全文可见，实验重点是跨模型族、跨尺度验证方法稳定性，以及拆解 RGSI 与 stage-wise training 各自的贡献。作者报告在多个开源模型上都能带来一致提升，尤其是在需要构造例子、反例或边界案例的数学题型上更明显。实验设计上，除了主结果，还做了几类关键消融：1）直接使用外部 reference 作为 chosen，与 RGSI 生成的 internalized response 对比，用来验证分布偏移问题；2）单阶段偏好训练与两阶段训练对比，用来验证 progressive acquisition 假设；3）只看 correctness rubric 与三维 rubric 对比，用来验证 method signal 的必要性；4）对 judge rubric 的维度贡献做分析，观察 Method 分数提升是否先于 Correctness 提升。你给出的全文片段没有包含完整表格数字、参数量和全部 benchmark 名称，因此无法负责任地填入具体提升幅度。但从论文叙述看，作者强调的是‘consistent improvements across multiple model scales and families’以及消融结果对设计选择的支持，而不是单一 benchmark 上的大幅跃升。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议是先看 Introduction 和 Figure 2，抓住作者到底在解决什么：不是一般数学推理增强，而是 example-driven reasoning 的能力形成。然后重点看 3.1 的 rubric 设计和 RGSI 数据构造，这里决定了这篇工作的成败。读的时候要特别留意一个问题：internalization 具体如何约束学生既吸收参考策略、又保持自身分布风格；如果这一步约束不强，方法就容易退化成 reference imitation。接着看 3.2 的 stage-wise preference training，关注两个阶段的目标差异、pair 构造方式、以及训练切换条件。实验部分建议先看主表，再看 ablation，尤其是 direct-reference vs RGSI、single-stage vs stage-wise、correctness-only vs rubric-based 这几组。预计 25–35 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读；如果你关心 reasoning post-training 或 curriculum design，可以再深看附录里的 rubric prompt 和案例分析。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a narrower but important gap in mathematical reasoning: models may optimize for final-answer correctness without actually acquiring example-driven reasoning, such as constructing examples or counterexamples to probe the boundary of a claim. The authors argue that this capability is underdeveloped in current LLMs and hard to improve with standard preference optimization for two reasons. First, there is ability scarcity: on-policy samples from the base model are uniformly weak on this dimension, so they do not form informative preference pairs. Second, the capability is progressive: the model must first learn to adopt the strategy, and only then learn to apply it correctly.
summary_en.importance: Its value for pretraining-oriented readers is indirect but real. The paper is not about a new pretraining objective; it is about how capability acquisition can fail when the target behavior is absent from the current policy distribution. That makes it relevant to synthetic data generation, curriculum design, mid-training, and the interface between pretrain and post-train. The main lesson is practical: pure on-policy preference learning may not provide enough signal when the desired reasoning mode is rare, while directly using external high-quality references can introduce style and reasoning-structure mismatch. The paper proposes a middle path and frames the problem in a way that is useful beyond math reasoning.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method, INSPIRE, has two coupled components. The first is Reference-Guided Student Internalization (RGSI). Instead of directly treating an external reference solution as the preferred response, the model is asked to understand the reference reasoning pattern and regenerate an answer in its own style. This is meant to preserve the policy model’s distribution while injecting the missing example-based reasoning signal. The second is stage-wise rubric-based preference training. Rather than collapsing quality into answer correctness, the paper defines a three-dimensional rubric: Method, Reasoning, and Correctness. Method checks whether the response actively uses an example-based analytical strategy; Reasoning evaluates coherence and completeness; Correctness evaluates the final answer. DeepSeek V3.2 is used as the judge to score each dimension independently. Training is then staged: first encourage adoption of the strategy, then refine correctness on top of that. The key distinction from one-shot DPO-style training is that the paper explicitly treats capability acquisition as sequential rather than simultaneous.
summary_en.experiments: The experimental story is centered on consistency across model families and scales, plus ablations that isolate the contribution of RGSI and stage-wise training. According to the full text provided, the method improves performance consistently, with larger gains on problems where constructing examples, counterexamples, or boundary cases is especially relevant. The most important ablations compare: (1) direct external references as preferred samples vs RGSI-internalized responses, to test the distribution-shift hypothesis; (2) single-stage preference training vs the proposed staged training, to test the progressive-acquisition claim; (3) correctness-only preference signals vs the full rubric, to test whether method supervision matters; and (4) dimension-wise score trajectories, to see whether Method improves before Correctness. The excerpt does not include the full result tables, parameter counts, or exact benchmark numbers, so it would be unsafe to invent specific gains. The paper’s emphasis is on stable improvements and design validation rather than one headline metric.
summary_en.reading_guide: Start with the introduction and Figure 2. The central point is not generic math reasoning improvement, but the acquisition of example-driven reasoning as a distinct capability. Then read Section 3.1 carefully: the rubric design and RGSI data construction are where the paper stands or falls. A useful question while reading is whether the internalization step truly preserves the student model’s distribution, or whether it still collapses into reference imitation. After that, read Section 3.2 for the stage-wise preference setup, especially how the two stages differ in objective and pair construction. In the experiments, prioritize the main table and the ablations comparing direct-reference training, RGSI, single-stage training, and rubric variants. A solid skim should take about 25–35 minutes. If your interest is reasoning post-training or curriculum learning, the appendix prompts and qualitative case studies are worth extra time.

recommendation.zh: 这篇不直接改 pretrain，但“能力先内化、再优化”的分阶段假设值得拿去审视 R1 类配方；先看方法图和偏好对构造细节。
recommendation.en: It does not change pretraining directly, but the staged 'internalize first, optimize later' hypothesis is worth testing against R1-style recipes; start with the method diagram and preference-pair construction.

paper.title: From Atomic to Agentic: Towards Interpretable Evaluation of LLMs' Agentic Mathematical Capabilities
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are evolving from performing end-to-end mathematical reasoning to integrating agentic intelligence. However, most existing math benchmarks evaluate only final answers. This outcome-oriented evaluation provides limited diagnostic value for identifying process-level failures or rigorous logic, failing to guide the transformation of LLMs into robust agents. To bridge this gap, we present a process-level benchmark designed to evaluate the inherent agentic mathematical re

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的是：现有数学 benchmark 大多只看最终答案，对 agentic reasoning 的评估过于结果导向，无法区分模型到底是不会规划、不会执行某个原子能力，还是不会在中途发现并修正错误。作者关心的不是“端到端数学题能做对多少”，而是“基础模型是否已经具备可被 agent 框架调用的内在 agentic 数学能力”。因此他们把数学推理拆成原子能力，再把这些能力映射到 Planning、Action、Feedback 三类 agent 功能，做过程级、可诊断的评测。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对 pretrain-posttrain 接口有现实意义。现在很多推理增强、tool use、agent 框架把性能提升归因于系统设计，可如果底座模型在 planning、step execution、self-correction 上的能力分布并不均衡，后续训练和系统搭建就容易误判瓶颈。AMB 的价值在于把“数学能力”与“agentic 能力”做了结构化对齐，提供了更细粒度的 failure surface。对做 reasoning data synthesis、process supervision、RL for reasoning、verifier 或 curriculum 的人，这类 benchmark 能帮助判断该补的是原子执行能力、元认知能力，还是反馈修正能力。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上，论文先构建一个数学原子能力 taxonomy，再把它与 agent 功能轴对齐。数学能力分三层：Level 1 是基础概念与计算，包括符号识别、概念理解、计算；Level 2 是高级推理与应用，包括空间感知、形式化、演绎/归纳推理、数学建模；Level 3 是元认知，包括定理应用、自我反思、新知识学习。作者强调这不是简单给数学技能换标签，而是评估“能力 × agent 功能”的交叉点：Planning 关注能力选择、排序和下一步决策；Action 关注单个原子能力的独立执行；Feedback 关注对既有轨迹的监控、诊断与修正。数据构建方面，作者做了自动化 pipeline，包括数据收集、高质量 trajectory synthesis、多阶段过滤和细粒度标注，并覆盖 text-only 与 multimodal 场景。这个设计的关键取舍是把内在 agentic intelligence 与完整 agent system 解耦：不要求模型真的去调工具、跑环境，而是先测底座是否具备这些可复用的过程能力。这样评测更可控，也更容易定位短板。
summary.experiments: 从给出的全文片段看，实验主结论是：一些 end-to-end 数学表现接近的模型，在 AMB 上会呈现明显不同的 agentic profile，说明只看 final answer 会掩盖过程能力差异。论文还强调 benchmark 覆盖 planning、action、feedback 三类任务，并同时包含文本与多模态数学场景。当前可确认的实验信息主要是定性结论和 benchmark 设计，而不是具体榜单数字；如果阅读全文，建议重点查模型列表、任务规模、每个子能力的样本数、自动标注一致性、以及不同模型在三大功能轴上的分数分布。真正决定这篇 benchmark 是否站得住的，不是总分，而是：1）子任务是否足够去耦；2）自动构造的 trajectory 和标签是否可靠；3）过程级指标是否能预测真实 agent 系统中的失效模式。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合按 benchmark 论文的方式读。先看方法部分对 taxonomy 的定义，确认数学原子能力与 Planning/Action/Feedback 的映射是否清楚、是否有重叠。然后看数据构建 pipeline，尤其是 trajectory synthesis、过滤和标注规则，因为 benchmark 的可信度主要取决于这里。实验部分不要只看总榜，优先看各子能力、各 agent 功能维度的拆分结果，以及作者是否展示了“终局分数相近但过程画像不同”的案例。若时间有限，读引言、taxonomy 设计、数据构建和主实验图表即可，约 25 分钟。若要深挖，建议重点检查附录里任务定义、标注模板和 failure case，因为这决定它能否真正服务于 reasoning/post-training 研究，而不只是再多一个数学榜单。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a clear evaluation gap: most math benchmarks judge only the final answer, which makes them poor tools for diagnosing agentic reasoning. They cannot tell whether a model failed at planning, failed to execute a specific atomic skill, or failed to detect and revise an earlier mistake. The goal is therefore not to measure end-to-end math accuracy again, but to evaluate whether a base LLM already contains the intrinsic agentic capabilities needed for mathematical problem solving. To do that, the authors decompose math reasoning into atomic capabilities and align them with three agent functions: Planning, Action, and Feedback.
summary_en.importance: This is not a direct pretraining contribution, but it is relevant to the pretrain-to-posttrain interface. A lot of current progress in reasoning and agents is attributed to scaffolding, tool use, or system design. That can hide the actual bottleneck if the underlying model has uneven capability across planning, execution, and self-correction. AMB is useful because it turns that vague question into a structured evaluation surface. For work on reasoning data synthesis, process supervision, RL for reasoning, verifiers, or curricula, this kind of benchmark can help identify whether the missing ingredient is atomic execution skill, meta-cognitive control, or feedback-based revision.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark is organized around two aligned axes. On the math side, the authors define a taxonomy of atomic capabilities in three levels: Level 1 covers foundational concepts and calculation, including symbol recognition, concept understanding, and calculation; Level 2 covers advanced reasoning and application, including spatial perception, formalization, deductive and inductive reasoning, and mathematical modeling; Level 3 covers meta-cognition, including theorem application, self-reflection, and new knowledge learning. On the agent side, these are aligned with Planning, Action, and Feedback. The key point is that the benchmark evaluates the intersection rather than simply relabeling math skills: planning is framed as capability selection, ordering, and next-step decision making; action as isolated execution of a single atomic capability; feedback as monitoring and revising an existing trajectory. The dataset construction uses an automated pipeline with data collection, trajectory synthesis, multi-stage filtering, and fine-grained annotation, and it includes both text-only and multimodal settings. A notable design choice is to decouple intrinsic agentic evaluation from full agent deployment, so the benchmark measures reusable process capabilities without requiring a complete tool-using system.
summary_en.experiments: From the provided full-text excerpt, the main experimental claim is that models with similar end-to-end math performance can show substantially different agentic profiles on AMB. That is the central evidence for why process-level evaluation matters. The benchmark spans planning, action, and feedback tasks, and covers both textual and multimodal mathematical scenarios. The excerpt does not provide enough concrete numbers to report a reliable leaderboard summary, so the most important things to verify in the full paper are the model roster, task counts per capability, annotation quality, and score distributions across the three agent-function axes. The real test of the benchmark is not the aggregate score, but whether its subtask decomposition is clean, whether the automatically synthesized trajectories are trustworthy, and whether process-level scores correlate with failure modes in actual agent systems.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read this like an evaluation paper, not a methods paper. Start with the taxonomy and check whether the mapping from mathematical atomic skills to Planning/Action/Feedback is precise rather than hand-wavy. Then move to the data pipeline, especially trajectory synthesis, filtering, and annotation, because benchmark credibility depends on those details. In the experiments, do not stop at the overall ranking. Look for per-capability and per-agent-function breakdowns, and for examples where models with similar final-answer accuracy differ sharply in process-level behavior. If time is limited, the introduction, taxonomy design, data construction, and main result tables should be enough in about 25 minutes. For deeper reading, the appendix matters: task definitions, annotation templates, and failure cases will tell you whether this benchmark can genuinely support reasoning and post-training research, rather than just adding another math leaderboard.

recommendation.zh: 值得看，但别把它当数学 benchmark；重点是它把 agentic reasoning 拆成可训练、可验的原子能力，这会直接影响你怎么做 SFT/RL 数据分层。
recommendation.en: Worth reading, but not as just another math benchmark; the useful part is the decomposition of agentic reasoning into trainable and verifiable atomic skills, which should change how you tier SFT/RL data.

paper.title: DIAG: Diagnostic Iterative Alignment and Generation for Data-Efficient Mathematical Preference Distillation
paper.abstract: Iterative preference optimization is essential for aligning Large Language Models on mathematical reasoning tasks, yet its efficiency is often throttled by signal scarcity: as the model improves, static problem sets become increasingly mismatched to the model's evolving competence, producing rollouts that are either too easy or too hard and therefore non-informative, which leads to a scarcity of valid preference pairs. We propose DIAG, a Diagnostic Iterative Alignment and Generation framework th

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是在线数学偏好蒸馏里的一个数据效率问题：随着 student 变强，固定题库越来越不匹配当前能力边界，导致 rollouts 不是太容易就是太难，最终拿不到足够多“一个对、一个错”的自然偏好对。DPO 或其他 preference optimization 在数学任务上往往受限于这种 signal scarcity，而不是单纯受限于优化器或模型容量。DIAG 试图把这个问题显式建模成 practice distribution 的控制问题：每一轮训练后先诊断当前题目分布还能产出多少有效 preference pairs，再据此调整下一轮题目主题和难度，让生成集中在 student 的决策边界附近。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对 pretrain-posttrain 接口有现实意义。它提醒人注意一个常被忽略的事实：在线对齐或推理蒸馏的瓶颈，很多时候不是缺 teacher，也不是缺算力，而是缺“信息密度足够高的训练样本”。这个视角和持续预训练、mid-training、reasoning data synthesis 是相通的。若把数学偏好蒸馏换成更一般的能力蒸馏，DIAG 代表的是一种 signal-aware curriculum：不是盲目扩大数据池，而是根据当前模型错误分布去生成下一轮数据。这个思路对合成预训练数据、continual pretrain 中的数据配比、以及 RL/SFT 阶段如何避免样本过易或过难，都有启发。不过它仍然偏 post-train，且场景限定在可验证数学推理，外推到开放域任务时需要谨慎。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是 Diagnose-and-Generate 两阶段闭环。第一阶段 Diagnose & Allocate，目标是估计当前 practice distribution 的“有效监督产率”，也就是给定一批题目和当前 student，多大概率能采到既有正确轨迹又有错误轨迹的 rollout 集合，从而形成可用 preference pair。作者没有把 topic-level 统计直接拿来做硬决策，而是引入 Empirical Bayes shrinkage 来平滑低样本主题的估计，避免某些主题因为偶然几次高收益就被过度放大，或者因为样本太少被过早放弃。与此同时，系统会在 exploration 和 exploitation 之间做配额分配：一部分预算继续覆盖更广主题，防止课程塌缩；另一部分预算集中到当前高产率区域。

第二阶段是 mistake-conditioned generation。与其从静态候选池里做 active selection，DIAG 让 teacher 根据 student 最近的错误轨迹生成后续题目。这样生成出来的问题更贴近 student 当前失败模式，也更可能落在“差一点会、但还没完全会”的区域。文中还提到 uncertainty-weighted resampling，用来把计算预算进一步压到决策边界附近，而不是平均撒在所有主题上。

这个方法和传统 active learning 的区别在于，它不是从现成题库里挑高不确定样本，而是根据 student 的错误结构主动生成新题；和 brute-force 扩大 rollout width 的区别在于，它优先提高每个样本产生有效 preference signal 的概率，而不是单纯多采样。若从训练信号角度看，DIAG 关心的是 pair yield 和 pair quality 两件事：前者决定监督密度，后者决定偏好学习是否真的贴着能力边界发生。
summary.experiments:
从已给出的全文内容看，实验重点不是追求单次 benchmark 的绝对分数，而是证明 DIAG 在相同或更低预算下能产出更多有效 preference pairs，并把这些更高信息密度的样本转化为更好的数学推理性能。引言里明确声称：静态 practice distribution 会导致 natural contrastive supervision 快速下降；DIAG 通过 signal-aware pacing、Empirical Bayes topic scoring 和错误条件生成，提高了 preference-pair yield，并且单位预算的信息密度更高。

由于当前提供的正文片段没有完整实验表和具体数字，能确认的实验结论主要是方向性的：一，随着迭代进行，固定题库越来越难提供有效 pair；二，按 topic 做稳健配额分配优于直接按原始统计贪心采样；三，mistake-conditioned generation 比 practice-agnostic generation 更能贴近 student 的能力边界，因此更容易形成有区分度的偏好监督。若阅读全文，建议重点核对三类数字：每轮有效 pair 比例、总训练预算下的最终数学 benchmark 提升、以及不同 topic allocation 策略下的方差和稳定性。没有这些数字，很难判断它到底是“更省数据”还是只是“更会造题”。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先抓住一个主线：这不是在改 DPO 目标，而是在改 DPO 的数据生成闭环。先看 Introduction 和方法总图，理解作者为何把问题定义成 signal-yield problem。然后重点看 Diagnose & Allocate 的公式和算法，尤其是 Empirical Bayes shrinkage 如何处理低计数主题；再看 mistake-conditioned generation 的 prompt 设计和 uncertainty-weighted resampling。最后看实验里关于 pair yield 随迭代变化的曲线，这比最终 benchmark 分数更能说明方法是否成立。

预计 15 到 25 分钟可以完成有效泛读。若要继续深挖，建议重点问四个问题：一，valid preference pair 的判定是否依赖可验证答案，因此方法是否只适用于数学这类可判题任务；二，teacher 根据 student 错误生成新题时，是否会逐渐收缩到狭窄题型，造成泛化下降；三，Empirical Bayes 的先验设定对 topic allocation 有多敏感；四，pair yield 提高后，最终收益来自更好的 curriculum，还是来自 teacher 生成题目本身更接近测试分布。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a data-efficiency bottleneck in online mathematical preference distillation. As the student improves, a fixed prompt pool becomes increasingly mismatched to the model’s competence boundary, so rollouts are often either too easy or too hard. In both cases, the system fails to produce enough natural preference pairs with one correct and one incorrect trajectory. DIAG reframes this as a curriculum-control problem: after each alignment round, diagnose how much usable preference signal the current practice distribution still yields, then reshape the next round of practice so that generation stays near the student’s decision boundary.
summary_en.importance: This is not a direct pretraining contribution, but it is relevant to the pretrain–posttrain interface. The paper highlights a practical point that often gets missed: in online alignment and reasoning distillation, the bottleneck is frequently not teacher quality or raw compute, but the density of informative supervision. That perspective transfers to synthetic data generation, continual pretraining, mid-training curricula, and reasoning-focused post-training. In a broader sense, DIAG is a signal-aware curriculum method: instead of scaling the prompt pool blindly, it adapts future data generation to the student’s observed failure modes. The caveat is that the current setting is verifiable mathematical reasoning, so generalization to open-ended domains is not automatic.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The method is a two-stage Diagnose-and-Generate loop. In the first stage, Diagnose & Allocate, the system estimates the effective supervision yield of the current practice distribution: given the current student and a set of prompts, how likely is it that sampled rollouts will contain both correct and incorrect trajectories, producing a usable preference pair? Rather than making topic-level decisions from raw counts, DIAG uses Empirical Bayes shrinkage to stabilize estimates under low sample counts. This prevents overreacting to noisy topics that happen to look good or bad due to small numbers. It also allocates budget between exploration and exploitation, so the curriculum does not collapse too early onto a narrow subset of topics.

In the second stage, the teacher generates follow-up problems conditioned on the student’s recent mistakes. This is the key departure from standard active learning. Instead of selecting uncertain prompts from a static candidate pool, DIAG actively creates new prompts that target the student’s current failure modes. The paper also uses uncertainty-weighted resampling to concentrate compute near the competence boundary rather than spreading it uniformly.

Conceptually, the method optimizes two quantities at once: pair yield and pair quality. Pair yield determines how much supervision is available per unit budget. Pair quality determines whether preference learning happens on examples that are actually informative for the current student. Compared with brute-force scaling of rollout width, DIAG tries to increase the probability that each sampled problem produces useful contrastive signal.
summary_en.experiments:
From the provided full-text content, the experimental emphasis is not on a single benchmark headline but on showing that DIAG produces more informative preference pairs under the same or lower budget, and converts that higher signal density into better mathematical reasoning performance. The introduction explicitly claims that static practice distributions cause a rapid decline in natural contrastive supervision, while DIAG improves preference-pair yield through signal-aware pacing, Empirical Bayes topic scoring, and mistake-conditioned generation.

Because the supplied text does not include the full result tables, the confirmed findings are directional rather than fully numeric. First, fixed prompt pools become less effective over iterations as the student improves. Second, robust topic allocation outperforms greedy allocation based on raw observed yields. Third, mistake-conditioned generation is better than practice-agnostic generation at staying near the student’s competence boundary, which increases the chance of obtaining discriminative preference supervision. When reading the full paper, the most important numbers to verify are: the valid-pair rate per iteration, final benchmark gains under matched training budgets, and the variance or stability of different topic-allocation strategies. Without those, it is hard to tell whether the method is truly data-efficient or simply benefits from stronger synthetic problem generation.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a skim, keep one thread in mind: the paper is not changing the DPO objective, it is changing the data-generation loop around DPO. Start with the introduction and the method overview to see why the authors cast the problem as signal yield. Then focus on the Diagnose & Allocate component, especially how Empirical Bayes shrinkage handles low-count topics. After that, read the mistake-conditioned generation setup and the uncertainty-weighted resampling mechanism. In the experiments, the most informative plots should be the curves showing how valid preference-pair yield evolves over iterations; those matter more than the final benchmark score alone.

A useful skim should take about 15 to 25 minutes. If reading more carefully, track four questions. Does the definition of a valid preference pair rely on verifiable answers, making the method specific to math-like domains? Does mistake-conditioned generation gradually narrow the curriculum too much and hurt generalization? How sensitive is topic allocation to the Empirical Bayes prior? And when performance improves, how much comes from better curriculum control versus the teacher generating prompts that are simply closer to the evaluation distribution?

recommendation.zh: 只看方法和数据选择 ablation；把 preference-pair yield 当课程信号这点值得在内部 RLVR 数据管线复现。
recommendation.en: Read the method and data-selection ablations; using preference-pair yield as a curriculum signal is worth reproducing in an internal RLVR pipeline.

paper.title: Hints, Critics, and Teachers: Prior Injection for Sparse-Reward RL in Vision-Language Math Reasoning

We train eleven methods under identical conditions in this regime, each injecting a different prior: text (reference-solution hints), distribution (on-policy distillation from a 7B teacher), and value (a value-pretrained critic with an MSE

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是一个很具体、也很常见的 RL 失效点：在视觉-语言数学推理里，如果基础模型初始成功率很低，GRPO 这类组内相对优势方法会因为“整组全错”而拿不到有效梯度，训练几乎处于饥饿状态。作者不是再提一个单点技巧，而是把三类常见补救思路放到同一控制条件下比较：文本先验（hint）、分布先验（teacher distillation）、价值先验（critic）。论文真正要回答的问题不是“哪种方法名字更好”，而是“先验是否真的传递到了 policy”，以及在极端 sparse-reward 条件下，哪些设计能把无梯度状态改造成可学习状态。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究者来说，这篇文章的价值不在 GUI 或 VLM 任务本身，而在它把 post-train RL 中一个常被模糊处理的问题拆开了：当 reward 太稀疏时，训练成败首先取决于训练信号能否穿透到 token 级更新，而不是取决于目标函数表面形式。这个结论对 reasoning RL、RLVR、以及更广义的 pretrain↔post-train 接口都有参考意义。第二个价值点是评测有效性：作者发现一个长期使用的 held-out 集合会系统性奖励“模型没变”，甚至与真实跨域迁移负相关，这对任何依赖固定验证集做 recipe 选择的训练工作都很重要。第三个价值点是工程验证：评分器、答案抽取器、judge 设计、porting bug 都可能比算法差异更大，论文把这些问题当作一等公民处理，这一点比很多方法细节更值得借鉴。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上，作者先构造并验证了一个真正稀疏的训练池：从 MathV360K 里筛出 20,830 个 visual-math 问题，用 Qwen2-VL-2B 预先测得单 rollout 正确率只有 3.6%，85%–97% 的 GRPO rollout group 全错。然后在完全相同的训练预算、数据池、随机种子和硬件条件下，比较 11 个训练臂。文本先验部分，核心是给模型前缀一段参考解法，让采样从更接近成功的状态开始；作者还区分了“hint 真正改善探索”与“UFT 类辅助似然项是否额外有用”，结论是收益主要来自探索起点改变，而不是额外的监督项。分布先验部分，作者比较了多种 on-policy distillation 方式，关键差别在于 teacher 信号是否被 teacher 能力上限卡住、是否只在失败样本上 gated、以及是否随训练退火；结果显示 annealed global distillation 有效，而 failure-gated persistent distillation 不行，说明蒸馏信号如果只在局部失败区域触发，往往送不到真正决定策略迁移的地方。价值先验部分，作者训练 critic 给 token 级 credit assignment，但重点不是“有没有 critic”，而是 critic 的参数化是否正确：把 clipped-MSE 标量回归换成 HL-Gauss categorical loss 之后，credit 传播质量明显改善。作者把这个变化描述为一行替换，但含义很重：在稀疏奖励下，value head 的表示形式会直接决定先验是否能被 policy 吸收。最后还测试了 text prior 和 distribution prior 叠加，发现几乎没有叠加收益，说明二者主要都在解决同一个早期瓶颈，而不是互补瓶颈。
summary.experiments: 实验设计很干净。11 个 arms 用同一训练池、同一步数和 batch 预算、同一 seed、每个 arm 一台 8×A800 节点。评测采用独立 LLM judge（DeepSeek）盲评完整输出，并用 McNemar exact test 做成对显著性检验。核心结果有三层。第一层是“先验是否送达”的分层：在训练域外的 DynaMath 上，6 个先验确实传到 policy 的方法集中在 30.6%–32.9%，其余 5 个方法——包括 plain GRPO 和几种先验被 teacher cap、gating 或 critic 失配吞掉的变体——集中在 27.0%–29.1%，两组区间不重叠。第二层是组件级归因：hint 预验证可把成功率从 7.2% 拉到 34.4%，说明探索起点确实能解锁稀疏任务；critic 从 clipped-MSE 改成 HL-Gauss 后，in-domain accuracy 提升 +14.4 个百分点，并把原本最弱的训练臂变成第二好的 cross-domain 臂；双先验叠加没有额外收益。第三层是评测集诊断：旧的 held-out 集 old-319 与真实跨域迁移排名呈负相关，Spearman ρ=-0.74；最难的 in-domain 子集 sparse-800 与迁移呈强正相关，ρ=+0.89。作者进一步分析 old-319 中 69% 是四选一选择题，各方法都接近 25% 猜测下限，因此“保持输出短选项字母”的旧行为反而拿高分，导致它奖励模型不发生能力变化。论文还做了 scoring audit，发现启发式答案抽取器会对不同方法造成最高 30 个百分点的系统偏差，甚至能颠倒排序；同时排查了 guessing 和 format reward hacking，认为主结果不是这些伪因素造成的。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时先看 Introduction 和方法总表，抓住作者的主线：不是比较三类先验谁名义上更强，而是比较“先验有没有真正进入 policy 更新”。然后重点看结果部分里对 11 个 arms 的分组结果，以及 critic loss 那一节；这是最有信息量的地方。评测部分建议至少认真看 old-319 与 sparse-800 的相关性分析，因为它解释了为什么一个看似正常的 held-out 集会把实验方向带偏。工程上值得看 Section 6 一类的 verification protocol，包括 blind judge、scoring audit、bug gating，这部分对做 RL 训练的人很实用。作为 skim 级阅读，建议 25–35 分钟：先读引言、主结果图表、critic loss 对比、evaluation validity 分析，最后扫一遍附录里评分与审计细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a concrete failure mode of GRPO-style RL in vision-language math reasoning: when the base policy almost never solves a problem, most rollout groups are entirely wrong, the group-relative advantage becomes zero, and training receives no useful gradient. The real question is not which family of tricks sounds better, but which kind of prior actually reaches the policy under extreme sparse-reward conditions. The authors compare three families under matched settings: text priors via hints, distribution priors via teacher distillation, and value priors via a critic.
summary_en.importance: Its relevance goes beyond this specific VLM math setup. For anyone working on reasoning RL, RLVR, or the pretrain-to-post-train interface, the paper makes a sharp point: under sparse rewards, progress depends first on whether learning signal can penetrate token-level updates, not on the nominal form of the objective. A second contribution is methodological: the paper shows that a commonly used held-out set can systematically reward models for not changing, and can even anti-correlate with true cross-domain transfer. That is directly relevant to recipe selection and ablation practice. A third contribution is experimental discipline. Scoring bugs, answer extraction heuristics, and judge design can dominate algorithmic differences; the paper treats these as first-class objects rather than afterthoughts.
summary_en.technical_approach: The setup starts with a deliberately sparse training pool: 20,830 visual-math problems filtered from MathV360K, where Qwen2-VL-2B gets only 3.6% rollout accuracy and 85%–97% of GRPO groups are all-wrong. On this pool, the authors train 11 arms under identical data, budget, seed, and hardware conditions. For text priors, they prepend part of a reference solution so exploration starts from a more promising state. An important decomposition is that the gain comes from improved exploration itself, while the auxiliary UFT-style likelihood term adds little. For distribution priors, they compare several on-policy distillation variants and show that delivery matters: if the signal is capped by teacher ability, gated only to failures, or otherwise poorly routed, it does not help much. Annealed global distillation works; failure-gated persistent distillation does not. For value priors, they train a critic to provide token-level credit assignment even when sequence-level outcomes are uniform. The key finding is not merely that a critic helps, but that critic parameterization matters a lot: replacing clipped MSE scalar regression with an HL-Gauss categorical loss substantially improves signal delivery. They also test stacking text and distribution priors and find little additive benefit, suggesting both mainly address the same early bottleneck rather than complementary ones.
summary_en.experiments: The experimental design is unusually controlled: same pool, same step and batch budget, same seed, one 8×A800 node per arm. Evaluation uses blind judging by an independent LLM judge (DeepSeek) over full outputs, with McNemar exact tests for pairwise claims. The main result is a clean separation by signal delivery. On the out-of-domain DynaMath benchmark, the six arms whose prior demonstrably reaches the policy score 30.6%–32.9%, while the remaining five arms, including plain GRPO and variants where the prior is blocked or misparameterized, score 27.0%–29.1%, with no overlap. Component-level findings are also concrete. A half-solution hint raises prevalidated success from 7.2% to 34.4%, showing that exploration state matters. Changing the critic loss from clipped MSE to HL-Gauss yields +14.4 points in-domain and turns the weakest trained arm into the second-best cross-domain arm. Combining two priors brings little extra gain. The evaluation analysis is equally important: the old held-out set old-319 anti-correlates with genuine cross-domain transfer at Spearman rho = -0.74, while the hardest in-domain slice sparse-800 predicts transfer well at rho = +0.89. The proposed mechanism is compositional: 69% of old-319 is four-option multiple choice, where all methods sit near the 25% guessing floor, so models that preserve the base model’s short option-letter behavior score better. The paper also reports a scoring audit showing that a heuristic answer extractor can introduce up to 30-point arm-dependent bias and even invert rankings.
summary_en.reading_guide: For a quick but useful read, start with the introduction and the table of training arms. The central lens is simple: compare not whether a prior is nominally injected, but whether it is actually delivered to policy updates. Then read the main results section that groups the 11 arms by delivered versus undelivered prior, and the critic-loss comparison in detail. Those are the most informative parts. The evaluation-validity section deserves attention as well, especially the old-319 versus sparse-800 correlation analysis, because it explains how a plausible held-out set can steer conclusions in the wrong direction. The verification section is also worth scanning for practical RL work: blind LLM judging, scoring audits, and bug gating are all concrete and reusable. As a skim paper, this is about a 25–35 minute read if you focus on the setup, the main comparison figures, the critic ablation, and the evaluation audit.

recommendation.zh: 系统对比了稀疏奖励下 RL 的先验注入策略，结论清晰：先验必须直接作用于 policy 才有收益，且指出了评测集过拟合的坑，对做 RL post-training 的同学很有参考价值。
recommendation.en: Systematically compares prior injection strategies for RL under sparse rewards, concluding that priors must directly affect the policy to be beneficial, and highlights the pitfall of evaluation set overfitting; highly relevant for RL post-training.

paper.title: OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?
paper.abstract: We construct OEIS Open, a benchmark based on 492 open mathematical conjectures from the OEIS, formalized in Lean by Tsoukalas et al. Whereas these conjectures had previously been attempted only with a bespoke agent, our open-source evaluation code runs any generic language model (LM) against them, and is secure against LM cheating attempts. We find that LMs equipped with a minimal set of tools resolve 147 of these conjectures with a budget of \$50 per attempt, scoring 30% on OEIS Open. OEIS Open

summary.core_problem: 现有开放数学问题基准（HorizonMath、FrontierMath:OP）依赖生成器-验证器缺口，只能覆盖少数可构造可计算验证的问题，验证结果只是证据而非严格证明，且每个问题需要手工编写验证器、存在高比例不可解问题；同时近期AI解决开放数学问题的案例缺乏系统的成功率、成本和模型对比数据。需要一个覆盖更广、验证可靠、可系统比较通用LM能力的开放数学问题基准。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的价值在于提供了一个训练数据不会泄漏的、基于形式化证明的开放问题评测集，可用于衡量模型在数学推理前沿的真实能力边界，也可作为RL推理、推理时搜索、工具使用等后训练方法的硬评测基准；开放的评测脚手架也降低了不同模型和agent在同一任务上横向对比的成本。
summary.technical_approach: 基于OEIS的整数序列开放猜想，使用已有的Lean形式化结果构建基准：从2649条OEIS开放猜想中筛选500条非平凡、适合自动定理证明的问题，经Gemini agent形式化为Lean，排除8条技术问题后得到492条猜想构成OEIS Open，再随机抽取100条构成低成本子集OEIS Open Lite。评测要求模型在Lean中证明猜想或其否定，正确性由Lean内核保证，避免手工验证器的漏洞；同时设计防作弊机制，支持任意通用LM接入。评测时给模型配备最小工具集（Lean证明环境、搜索等），按单次尝试预算控制成本。
summary.experiments: 在50美元/次尝试预算下，带最小工具集的LM可解决492条中的147条，OEIS Open上成功率30%；在200美元/次尝试预算下，当前最优模型在OEIS Open Lite（100条）上成功率44%；额外给模型接入47.6万篇arXiv数学文献作为检索源，未带来OEIS Open Lite上的性能提升。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读重点看Introduction中对现有开放问题基准缺陷的逐条分析，以及Methods中基准构建的筛选流程和Lean形式化的风险控制；附录可关注防作弊机制的具体实现和评测脚手架的使用方式；阅读时间约30-40分钟。
summary.authors_note: Epoch Research；基于Tsoukalas等人2026年的OEIS猜想形式化工作构建。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing open-problem math benchmarks such as HorizonMath and FrontierMath:OP rely on a generator-verifier gap, which limits coverage to a small subset of constructible, computationally checkable problems, yields only evidence rather than rigorous proof, requires hand-written verifiers per problem, and includes a high fraction of unsolvable items. Meanwhile, recent high-profile AI demonstrations on open math problems lack systematic measurement of success rates, cost, and cross-model comparability. A benchmark with broader coverage, reliable verification, and support for generic LM evaluation is needed.
summary_en.importance: For pretraining research, this benchmark provides a training-data-leakage-free evaluation set based on formal proofs to measure the real capability boundary of models at the frontier of mathematical reasoning. It also serves as a hard evaluation target for post-training methods including RL for reasoning, inference-time search, and tool use. The open evaluation scaffold lowers the cost of head-to-head comparison across different models and agents.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark is built on existing Lean formalizations of open conjectures about integer sequences from OEIS. From 2,649 open OEIS conjectures, 500 non-trivial problems suitable for automated theorem proving are selected and formalized in Lean via a Gemini-based agent; 8 items are excluded for technical reasons, leaving 492 conjectures as OEIS Open, with a random 100-item subset forming the cheaper OEIS Open Lite. Evaluation requires a model to prove either the conjecture or its negation in Lean, with correctness guaranteed by the Lean kernel instead of per-problem hand-crafted verifiers. Anti-cheating mechanisms are built in, and the scaffold accepts any generic language model. Models are evaluated with a minimal tool set under a fixed per-attempt cost budget.
summary_en.experiments: Under a $50 per-attempt budget, LMs with a minimal tool set resolve 147 out of 492 conjectures, reaching a 30% success rate on OEIS Open. Under a $200 per-attempt budget, the best current model reaches 44% on OEIS Open Lite. Augmenting models with retrieval over 476,000 arXiv mathematics papers does not improve performance on OEIS Open Lite.
summary_en.reading_guide: For a skim pass, focus on the Introduction's itemized analysis of limitations in existing open-problem benchmarks, and the Methods section covering the selection pipeline and misformalization risk control via integer-sequence conjectures. The appendix is useful for details on anti-cheating mechanisms and the evaluation scaffold. Estimated reading time: 30-40 minutes.
summary_en.authors_note: Epoch Research; built on the 2026 OEIS conjecture formalization work by Tsoukalas et al.

recommendation.zh: 基于开放数学猜想的干净评测基准，完美规避数据污染，可用于预训练数学能力的 unbiased 评估，重点看评测协议设计。
recommendation.en: Clean math reasoning benchmark based on open conjectures, free of data contamination; useful for unbiased evaluation of pretrained math capability, focus on the evaluation protocol.

paper.title: FaithformBench: Benchmarking Faithfulness of Mathematical Chain-of-Thought Autoformalisation
paper.abstract: Autoformalisation (AF) systems map natural language reasoning steps into formal statements in a proof assistant such as Lean. We consider how to assess the faithfulness of these systems. Existing approaches require expensive human-annotated ground truth, or rely on LLM judges or embedding models, which come with limited guarantees of accuracy.
